children: A rise in goods prices triggered by higher oil costs will likely lift Japan's inflation going forward, says Mizuho Securities' Ryosuke Katagi. The economist expects surging packaging and material costs to push food inflation higher. "Stripping out special factors like government energy support, core consumer inflation will likely stay elevated in the low 3% range into early 2027," he says. "After that, Japan's inflation is expected to peak as cost pressures from high energy prices gradually fade, returning to around the [central bank's] 2% target in early 2028," he adds. The core measure, which excludes fresh food prices, climbed 2.2% from a year earlier in October, Friday's data showed. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)
